purpose: Test PPO exploration persistence at one million live transitions on three fresh training seeds with paired full initial parameters and own-initial controls.

evaluation.checkpoint_selection: First saved checkpoint at/above the threshold, within one rollout; final is the registered full budget, never a best checkpoint.
evaluation.classical: Fixed controller with both filters, rerun per row on the same Linux environment; never tuned.

scheduling: First training row gates the other five on technical success, never physical score. One GPU task at a time. CPU evaluations use separate allocations; final analysis requires all six completed rows.
limitations: Exploratory extension of an outcome-selected recipe that failed its restricted-area screen; this does not declare a candidate safe or competitive.
All three fresh cluster training seeds and both timing arms are required in the primary analysis; no selection of only successful runs.
Both arms use the same eight workers, CUDA device, batch size, rewards, source and initial tensors within each seed. Only gSDE resampling frequency differs.
Compared with the local pilot, workers, batch size, device, seed and budget change. Cross-study differences cannot isolate extra training alone.
Noise resampling changes both heading and speed correlation; the .01 value is noise-matrix weight std, not marginal action std.
The fixed KL stopping rule can yield different optimizer-step counts; actual counts and full-budget fractions must be reported.
Route guidance and static filtering stay on; traffic-conflict filtering stays off.
Twenty reused development worlds do not establish unseen generalization. Reserved20301/20302 and official42 remain unused.
The fixed classical system includes traffic filtering and is context, not a matched learning control.
No automatic promotion; apply the unchanged multi-metric screen to each seed and the three-seed mean, retain failures.
failure_behavior: Stop on failed checks or incomplete budgets; preserve all artifacts and do not overwrite or resubmit automatically.
